historical_reviews.deepseek: It identifies the read endpoint but preserves `-k`, password-style basic auth and no HTTP/status/schema oracle.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly changes classification and treats trust/credentials as prerequisites rather than a blocker.
historical_reviews.history: The invalidated prior-run location was searched and excluded as authority; the preceding DCMI temperature case and next AccountService resource were compared only to isolate protocol and resource coverage.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Pretty JSON from a reachable HTTPS socket does not prove a trusted Redfish ServiceRoot; transport identity, status, media type, schema and canonical links are independent gates.

original_test_intent: Retrieve the Redfish ServiceRoot from the intended BMC, prove trusted authenticated service availability and validate its version and canonical top-level resource links without modifying Redfish state.
original_method: Retain one GET to /redfish/v1 and JSON capture, replacing embedded credentials and unapproved TLS bypass with a target-bound trust/secret package and field/schema-aware acceptance.
manual_activity: The BMC/security owner approves the exact endpoint, least-privilege credential source, CA/certificate trust policy and any isolated-lab TLS exception; the project supplies the target Redfish schema/profile.
required_inputs: BMC hostname/IP bound to immutable SUT identity
Approved CA bundle or pinned certificate identity
Redfish/OData ServiceRoot schema and project profile
Required RedfishVersion, Systems and Managers link rules
safety_requirements: Keep credentials and Authorization headers out of argv/logs
Fail closed on redirect, certificate or target mismatch
No account, configuration, reset, power or firmware mutation
agent_execution_scope: Bind HTTPS endpoint and certificate to intended BMC
Capture status, headers and full body
Validate media type and JSON syntax
engineer_actions: Approve endpoint, credential and trust method
Provide schema/profile requirements and isolated-lab exception if needed

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its GET targets the right resource, but `-k` defeats endpoint authentication, `-u` can expose secret handling, and selecting three values loses the full document and HTTP evidence needed for conformance.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using approved certificate trust and secret-safe authentication, issue one bounded GET to https://<BMC>/redfish/v1, capture status/headers/full JSON, validate ServiceRoot schema plus RedfishVersion, Systems and Managers links, and archive only redacted evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source path, GET intent and 15/10 timing remain; no credential, CA exception or expected version is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat ServiceRoot discovery as a trusted API-contract check: independently bind target/certificate, authenticate through a secret provider, preserve the full response and validate transport, media, schema, version and canonical links.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes embedded password/unapproved TLS bypass and replaces readability with measurable protocol and schema acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Checking AccountService later does not prove ServiceRoot discovery or complete top-level link exposure; selecting only three fields hides malformed or contradictory metadata.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An untrusted endpoint can return plausible JSON while harvesting credentials; privileged basic-auth material can leak in process or logs; vendor extensions require an approved schema profile rather than silent rejection.

project_override_considerations: Session tokens or a Redfish client library are preferred only when certificate identity, least privilege, full response/schema validation and redacted evidence are preserved; any TLS exception must be explicit and recorded.
expected_evidence: Immutable SUT/BMC endpoint and certificate/trust result
Credential-provider and client/parser versions without secret material
Request timestamp plus HTTP status and relevant headers
Validated Systems and Managers link objects and resolvability
No Redfish mutation or log clearing

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, path and GET procedure consistently describe ServiceRoot retrieval. Hardcoded credentials, TLS bypass and readability-only criteria are unsafe/incomplete method details, not contradictions in the Master operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The endpoint and read purpose are explicit. Credentials, trust bundle, schema/profile and approval are concrete prerequisites; only unresolved identity or incompatible/non-Redfish responses after supply would block execution.

review_improvement: Converts an insecure pretty-print command into a trusted, credential-safe and schema-verifiable ServiceRoot contract check.
independent_technical_reasoning: `curl -k` removes the certificate identity proof that distinguishes the intended BMC from a wrong or intercepted endpoint, while privileged basic authentication magnifies that risk. Separately, `jq` producing readable text proves only JSON syntax. Redfish availability requires a successful HTTP response with appropriate media, a coherent ServiceRoot/OData identity, supported RedfishVersion and valid top-level links; all must be preserved without logging the credential.
